reason: README documents a CLI that separates a bundled test.mp3 into stems on CPU with freely downloadable models.
goal: Install demucs from the /work/demucs clone (CPU-only PyTorch) and run the CLI `python3 -m demucs --two-stems=vocals -d cpu -o OUTDIR test.mp3` on the bundled /work/demucs/test.mp3 with the default htdemucs model. It must download the pretrained weights and write separated stem wav files (vocals.wav and no_vocals.wav) under OUTDIR/htdemucs/test/.
check: The hidden test runs the separation on the bundled test.mp3 and verifies the stem wav files exist with plausible size and duration.

revision.by: second review (outside the maintained set; independent log check of maintained passes)
issues: Output content is not checked: v1 only asserts file size >500 kB, duration >5 s and 2 channels, which any 20 s stereo wav passes (e.g. a broken model emitting noise or silence). v2 checks the README's 44.1 kHz stereo format, that no_vocals is not silent, that stem length equals the input, and that vocals + no_vocals reconstructs test.mp3 (corr > 0.8), since no_vocals is the sum of the other stems.
evidence: src/facebookresearch-demucs/README.md:189,196-197,202 - `python3 -m demucs`, `--two-stems=vocals`, `-d cpu`; README.md:205-209 - stems are stereo 44.1 kHz int16 wav
src/facebookresearch-demucs/demucs/separate.py:208-218 - no_{stem} is the sum of the other sources (two-stems 'add' mode is the default)
src/facebookresearch-demucs/demucs/api.py:210-239 - mix loading: ffmpeg AudioFile first, torchaudio fallback (v2 does the same)
logs/facebookresearch-demucs/oracle.txt - 'vocals 20.0 2', 'no_vocals 20.0 2'; test.mp3 is 20.0 s; running from /work/demucs is fine because the clone is the editable-installed package
v2's numeric block was dry-run on synthetic stems (reconstruction corr 1.0)
